column1: Why can pip never repair a broken Python installation?
column2: pip is a Python package living inside that installation, so pip needs the very interpreter it would have to fix.

column1: Where does pip actually live on disk?
column2: Inside a Python installation, in site-packages, alongside every other installed package.

column1: What language is uv written in, and why does that matter?
column2: Rust. uv is a compiled binary that needs no interpreter to start, so it can install Python itself.

column1: State the chicken-and-egg idea in one line.
column2: A tool that installs Python cannot itself require Python.

column1: What installs uv on macOS or Linux?
column2: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

column1: What installs uv on Windows?
column2: powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

column1: What do the flags in curl -LsSf mean?
column2: -L follow redirects, -s stay quiet, -S still show real errors, -f fail properly on a bad response.

column1: Why is pip install uv the route to avoid?
column2: It puts uv inside a Python environment, which is the thing uv exists to manage from outside — and uv self update then fails.

column1: Which install routes support uv self update?
column2: Only the standalone installer routes. A pip-installed uv cannot replace its own file.

column1: You installed uv and the terminal says command not found. What happened?
column2: Your open shell read its PATH before uv existed. Open a new terminal.

column1: What is PATH?
column2: The short, ordered list of folders your shell searches for a command, using the first match it finds.

column1: Where does the standalone installer put the uv binary?
column2: ~/.local/bin on Unix, and the equivalent local bin folder on Windows.

column1: What three facts are in the uv --version output?
column2: The version number, the exact commit the binary was built from, and the build date.

column1: Which command shows where uv keeps its downloads?
column2: uv cache dir

column1: Which command shows where uv keeps installed tools?
column2: uv tool dir

column1: Which command shows where uv keeps downloaded interpreters?
column2: uv python dir

column1: How do you uninstall uv completely?
column2: uv cache clean, then delete the tool and python directories, then delete the uv and uvx binaries.

column1: Does installing uv change your existing Python?
column2: No. uv does not modify your system Python, your existing environments, or add a bare python to PATH.

column1: Compare pip and uv by where each one lives.
column2: pip lives inside a Python installation and depends on it. uv sits beside Python as an independent binary.

column1: Why can uv download a whole CPython on demand while pip cannot?
column2: uv starts without an interpreter, so fetching one is an ordinary download rather than a bootstrap problem.
